earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog: Capell 1940 contains 'the only published Gadjerong vocabulary'; extinct, no grammatical/phonological description exists.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record gadj1243 and reference list (Capell 1940; ISO CR 2019-006; Bowern 2011 list; UNESCO Atlas; Ethnologue; Austlang; Barker 2004).
sources.note: No grammar, sketch or phonology reference listed (n descriptive refs = 0); Glottolog comment: Capell 1940 contains the only published Gadjerong vocabulary.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1940. The classification of languages in north and north-west Australia. Oceania 10(3):241-272; 10(4):404-433.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only an areal remark covering all north/north-west Australian languages surveyed: 'Accent is also important, though it is difficult to set down rules for it.' Gadjerong appears only in a few example words/sentences (interdental stop, verb forms); no language-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Mirima Dawang Woorlab-gerring Language and Culture Centre website (mirima.org.au: home, resources, learning-resources, site search 'Gajirrabeng').
sources.note: No Gajirrabeng dictionary, grammar or learner's guide offered publicly; only Miriwoong materials listed.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2019. Change Request 2019-006 [gdh] Gadjerawang -> Gajirrabeng (submitted by Frances Kofod, supported by Knut Olawsky). SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Useful as a bibliographic pointer: cites 'Gajirrabeng-English Dictionary with English finder list and summary of grammar, Frances Kofod with Keeley Palmer and Gajirrabeng elders, Mirima Dawang Woorlab-gerring, Kununurra WA (ms for distribution to community members only) 2007' and states Kofod has recorded the language since 1971.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Gajirrawoong language' (cites Austlang K37.1, McGregor 2004, ABS census, WOLD).
sources.note: No phonology section; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: McGregor, William. 1988. Handbook of Kimberley Languages, Volume 1: General information. Pacific Linguistics C-105. Canberra: ANU. Section 3.6 'Gajirrawoong / Gadjerong', pp. 45-46.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Bibliographic handbook entry only: '6 Word lists: Capell (1940)', '7 Textual material: None published', '8 Grammar or sketch grammar: None, but Kofod is in the process of preparing a sketch grammar.'

sources.citation: Kofod, Frances. (in prep., reported 1988) Sketch grammar of Gajirrawoong. Unpublished notes/ms (McGregor 1988:45: 'Kofod is in the process of preparing a sketch grammar').
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: If it exists in AIATSIS or Mirima holdings it would be the only grammar sketch; status unknown.

sources.citation: Kofod, Frances & Knut Olawsky (depositors). 2020. Boorrb-goo jemang joodi-joodib ngalamberrmi: Gajirrabeng documentation. Endangered Languages Archive deposit 0573 (ELDP MDP0384): Toolbox lexicon PDF exports, 'Preliminary Grammar' elicitation bundles, 17 documents.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Primary corpus (95 h audio, ELAN/Toolbox files, lexicon PDFs); document bundles may include the 2007 dictionary front matter or grammar notes; audio would allow instrumental verification of stress.

sources.citation: Kofod, Frances, with Keeley Palmer and Gajirrabeng elders. 2007. Gajirrabeng-English Dictionary with English finder list and summary of grammar. Kununurra, WA: Mirima Dawang Woorlab-gerring (ms, community distribution only).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only known grammar summary of Gajirrabeng by the sole long-term fieldworker (recording since 1971); a pronunciation/orthography section would be the first-hand place for a stress statement.

sources.citation: McGregor, William B. 2004. The Languages of the Kimberley, Western Australia. London/New York: RoutledgeCurzon. (phonetics/phonology chapter)

sources.note: Standard areal survey covering Jarrakan incl. Gajirrawoong; its phonology chapter gives general Kimberley word-stress patterns and may note Miriwoong/Gajirrawoong specifics (second-hand at best).

sources.citation: Kofod, Frances M. 1978. The Miriwung language (East Kimberley): a phonological and morphological study. MA thesis, University of New England, Armidale.

sources.note: Full phonology (incl. stress) of Miriwoong (miri1266), the closest sister language in the Miriwoongic subgroup, by the same fieldworker; the natural comparandum and the likely template for any Gajirrabeng stress statement. Note: describes a different glottocode.
